doc.summary: Read docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md in full (HEAD, post-#317 state) and src/rights-model-identifiers.spec.ts in full, plus gh issue 320's body. Six findings below cover: §1/§2 rule-count, next-free ER id + block template, ER-1/ER-3 full text + cross-ref syntax gap, guard-spec INVENTORY/PAIRS mechanics, the presupposition sweep, and ER-16 confirmation.

findings.topic: 1. §1 operative sentences and rule count
findings.fact: §1 ('Three property buckets, built at WRITE time') holds two discrete, separable rules. Rule (i) — structure: line 33 'Every entity write runs aggregateEntity (utils/aggregate.js), which materializes three property objects on the stored document', plus line 35 '`propertiesToEntity` seeds `private`/`domain`/`public` as empty objects plus an `access` array (aggregate.js:312-320)' and line 36 'All actual property values always populate `private`. `domain` and `public` are selectively populated copies (§3).' Rule (ii) — write-time snapshot semantics: line 38 'The buckets are **snapshots taken at write time**, not computed at read time. This is the single most important structural fact: a read returns whatever was last written into these objects.' Neither carries an ER id today. Both are presupposed by ER-1 and ER-3 (and by §3's whole cap-logic exposition), matching the issue's own framed split (write-time-snapshot vs three-buckets-structure).
findings.evidence: Lines 31-40 of the doc, quoted verbatim above with line numbers.

findings.topic: 1. §2 operative sentences and rule count
findings.fact: §2 ('Read returns EXACTLY ONE bucket') also holds two discrete rules. Rule (i) — exactly-one-bucket selection + fallback: line 44 'cleanupEntity (utils/entity.js:569-612) selects one bucket by reader tier', the if/else code block (lines 47-55: grant→private, domain-access→domain, public-access→public, else return undefined), and line 58 'First match wins. The route handler turns the undefined return into 403 "No accessible properties" (routes/[db]/entity/[_id]/index.get.js:97-102).' Rule (ii) — the specific tier-priority order (grant > domain > public, first-match-wins) is a separable claim from 'exactly one bucket is returned' in the abstract. I checked whether tier-priority-order already has an ER id from #317: it does NOT. No existing ER block states the grant>domain>public ordering as its own citable claim — ER-1 is scoped to §3's three-gate exposure-AND (a different mechanism, for tier-admitted readers only), and ER-4 contrasts tier-admitted vs grant-admitted formulas without itself stating or naming the priority order. Line 60's 'Why private is robust' paragraph is explanatory detail (getAccessArray literal-push mechanics) supporting rule (i)/(ii), not a third separable rule with independent citations.
findings.evidence: Lines 42-60 of the doc; ID sweep via `grep -n '\*\*ER-'` confirmed no block text names/states the grant>domain>public order.

findings.topic: 2. Next free ER id
findings.fact: Highest currently-defined ER id is ER-17 (blocks ER-1 through ER-17 exist, no gaps, no duplicates, confirmed by extracting and sorting every `**ER-<n>**` definition-line token in the doc). Next free id is ER-18.
findings.evidence: `grep -n '\*\*ER-' docs/architecture/entu-rights-and-visibility-model.md | grep -o 'ER-[0-9]*' | sort -t- -k2 -n -u` returned ER-1..ER-17 with none repeated and none skipped.

findings.topic: 2. Exact block format at HEAD (verbatim template)
findings.fact:
Two verbatim templates, one with a Qualifications line and one without. WITH Qualifications (ER-6, lines 206-208): '> **ER-6** — A reference can hold at most one active direct rights-tier grant per entity. Granting a new direct tier (`_owner`/`_editor`/`_viewer`/`_expander`) for a reference that already holds a direct tier on that same entity retires (soft-deletes) the old one — even via a bare, independent POST carrying no prior `_id`.
> Evidence: `scripts/migrations/probes/probe-crede-editor-disappear-repro-2026-09-09.ts`, `scripts/migrations/probes/probe-entu-rights-supersession-cases-2026-09-09.ts`; results `scripts/migrations/seed-results/probe-crede-editor-disappear-repro-live-2026-09-09T16-56-49-211Z.json`, `scripts/migrations/seed-results/probe-entu-rights-supersession-cases-live-2026-09-09T17-04-41-123Z.json`.
> Qualifications: ER-8, ER-9.' WITHOUT Qualifications (ER-17, lines 141-142): '> **ER-17** — A `systemUser` (service-key) caller bypasses the `_owner` requirement of ER-11 on the WRITE path: the rights-property write check is skipped entirely for it. Claimed for the write path only — the DELETE gate (ER-11's DELETE citation) carries no such term.
> Evidence: `entity.js:115-121` — the `&& !entu.systemUser` term at `entity.js:116`; `entu-api` source-read 2026-09-10.' Format: bold id + em-dash + one-sentence-quotable-whole rule text; then an `> Evidence:` line (file:line, probe path, or `[unverified]`); optionally an `> Qualifications: ER-<n>, …` line naming every rule that bounds this one. A superseded block instead marks `(superseded by ER-<m>, <date>)` right after the bold id on the same first line (format asserted by the spec's fixture test, no live example currently in the doc).
findings.evidence: Doc lines 141-142 and 206-208, read directly.

findings.topic: 3. ER-1 and ER-3 full current text
findings.fact:
ER-1 (lines 94-96): '> **ER-1** — Bucket exposure is a three-gate AND, narrowest wins: (1) the prop-def's own `_sharing`, (2) the entity type's own `_sharing` as a cap, (3) the entity instance's own `_sharing` as a second retention gate. A property value reaches a **tier-admitted** reader — one admitted by the entity's `domain`/`public` sharing, holding no explicit rights grant — only if all three gates allow it. A reader admitted by an explicit grant is not bounded by these gates at all, and this formula does not hold for them: see ER-4.
> Evidence: aggregate.js:86,94,113-121 (gates 1–2); aggregate.js:269-275 (gate 3); synthesized in teams/mvox-dev/memory/perotin.md:1263-1272 (2026-08-08...); the omitted-gate re-widening this caused is scripts/migrations/lib/widen-member-refs-2026-08-07.ts. Distills §3; adds no new claim.
> Qualifications: ER-4.' ER-3 (lines 174-175): '> **ER-3** — A `_viewer`-alone grant already suffices for full private bucket read: property-tier `_sharing` (§3) does not filter on top of entity-level rights admission — entity rights decide the bucket, and the whole private bucket is exposed once any grant admits the caller to it.
> Evidence: scripts/migrations/probes/probe-294-entu-user-cross-admin-read-2026-09-08.ts; results scripts/migrations/seed-results/probe-294-entu-user-cross-admin-read-live-2026-09-08T10-15-15-643Z.json.' Both blocks cite §-numbers only in prose ('see §3'), never as a structural cross-reference line, and both currently presuppose §1/§2's mechanics silently (ER-1's 'tier-admitted' concept needs §2's bucket-selection; ER-3's 'entity rights decide the bucket... whole private bucket is exposed' needs §1's bucket-object existence and §2's grant-branch).
findings.evidence: Doc lines 94-96 and 174-175, read directly.

findings.topic: 3. Cross-reference syntax: only Qualifications: is defined; no 'presupposes'/'stands on' line exists
findings.fact: The scheme paragraph (line 27) verbatim: 'Where a rule carries a qualification — an exception, a boundary case, a direction it does not extend to — the qualification is itself a separately identified rule, and base and qualification name each other by ID: the qualification cites its base, and the base carries a `Qualifications: ER-<n>, …` line naming every rule that bounds it, so quoting the base whole shows that it is bounded. Never a clause, a parenthesis, or an "except" folded into the base rule's own sentence.' This paragraph defines exactly ONE structural cross-reference line type — `Qualifications:` — and it is semantically for bounding/exception relationships (base ← qualification), not for foundation/presupposition relationships (rule ← something it stands on, same direction as this issue's ER-1/ER-3 gap). No 'Presupposes:'/'Stands on:' line format is defined anywhere in the doc's scheme paragraph or elsewhere. The only other sanctioned mechanism is a bare `ER-<n>` token in ordinary prose (per the guard spec's own header comment, line 40: 'Write cross-reference lines as bare IDs — never restate the referenced rule's text') — but that instruction lives in the SPEC's comments, not in the doc's own normative scheme paragraph. So citing new §1/§2 foundation IDs from ER-1/ER-3 has no purpose-built line syntax to reuse; it would have to be a bare-ID mention inside the rule's existing sentence/evidence, or the team would need to newly define a 'Presupposes:'/'Foundations:' line convention (a gap, not something already specified).
findings.evidence: Doc line 27 (full scheme paragraph, quoted above verbatim); spec file line 40 comment; absence confirmed by scanning the doc for any line starting with a label other than 'Evidence:' or 'Qualifications:' preceding an ER token — none found.

findings.topic: 4. Guard spec INVENTORY array shape (2 entries quoted)
findings.fact: INVENTORY is `[string, RegExp[]][]`: label string + array of probe regexes, all of which must match a block's text for `blockMatching` to select it. Entry 'a': `['a. three visibility gates, narrowest wins', [/narrowest wins/i, /gate/i, /prop-def|property definition/i]]`. Entry 'm': `['m. changing _sharing requires _owner', [/_sharing/, /_owner/, /chang/i]]`. 14 entries total (a–n), each corresponding 1:1 to one of the amended-inventory rules from #317 + both Gama comments.
findings.evidence: spec lines 156-171, read directly.

findings.topic: 4. Guard spec PAIRS array shape (2 entries quoted)
findings.fact: PAIRS is an array of `{base, baseProbes, qual, qualProbes}` objects, each pointing at two INVENTORY probe-sets by index. Entry 1: `{ base: 'b (base replace rule)', baseProbes: INVENTORY[1][1], qual: 'c (propagation non-extension)', qualProbes: INVENTORY[2][1] }`. Entry 5: `{ base: 'm (changing _sharing requires _owner)', baseProbes: INVENTORY[12][1], qual: 'n (systemUser write-path bypass)', qualProbes: INVENTORY[13][1] }`. For each pair the spec asserts BOTH directions: the qualification's block text must contain the base's resolved id as a bare token (line 325-332), and the base block must carry a `Qualifications:` line (found by regex `^\s*Qualifications:/i` on a line within the block) that lists the qualification's id (line 334-349).
findings.evidence: spec lines 292-323 (PAIRS literal) and lines 325-349 (the two `it.each` assertions), read directly.

findings.topic: 4. What a new foundation rule + citations need in the spec
findings.fact: Section 1 tests (format well-formedness, id uniqueness, every bare ER-<n> token resolves to a defined block, no §-prefix/no-bracket) are fully generic over `blocks`/`doc` — a brand-new ER-18/ER-19 block for §1/§2, and any bare-token citation to them from ER-1/ER-3, is automatically checked by these tests with ZERO spec edits required. To get an INVENTORY-style 'this specific rule's content exists as exactly one block' coverage assertion (the pattern used for the #317/Gama amended list), the new foundation rules would need two new entries added to the INVENTORY array (label + distinctive-substring probe regexes) so `blockMatching` can find them — this is what the issue's third done-when checkbox ('the guard spec covers them like any other rule — well-formed, unique, every token resolving') is actually asking for, and per its own wording it stops at format/uniqueness/resolution, not full INVENTORY-coverage probes. If ER-1/ER-3 end up citing the new IDs via a genuinely new 'Qualifications:'-like line (rather than bare-prose tokens), that would ALSO need a new PAIRS entry to assert the bidirectional naming — but per finding above, no such line syntax is currently defined, so this only applies if the team invents one.
findings.evidence: spec lines 116-151 (section 1, generic over all blocks); spec lines 153-171 (INVENTORY, opt-in coverage); issue #320 body 'Done when' third bullet.

findings.topic: 5. Presupposition sweep — four-tier ladder (_viewer/_expander/_editor/_owner ordering)
findings.fact: No ER states the four-tier power-ranking (that _owner > _editor > _expander > _viewer, or any ordering among them) as its own rule. It is relied on by: ER-6/ER-9 ('a lower tier granted second retires a higher one' — needs a notion of which tier is 'lower'/'higher'), ER-5 ('aggregating as all four tiers' — needs the four-tier set), ER-7 ('the inherited layer carries no such constraint' on 'the direct layer is single-tier-per-reference' — needs the tier concept). §5 states the raw `rightTypes` array (`['_noaccess','_viewer','_expander','_editor','_owner','_sharing','_inheritrights']`, entity.js:21-29) as plain prose outside any blockquote — an enumeration, not a ranking, and not inside a citable ER block. Not citable today.
findings.evidence: ER-6 (lines 206-208), ER-9 (lines 216-217), ER-5 (lines 190-191), ER-7 (lines 210-211); §5 prose line 131 (rightTypes array, outside any blockquote).

findings.topic: 5. Presupposition sweep — direct-vs-inherited layer distinction
findings.fact: HAS an ER id already: ER-7 ('Direct and inherited rights are separate, additive layers on an entity's aggregated rights: direct grants follow ER-6; inherited grants cascade in via `_inheritrights` from parents (§1–§2). Only the direct layer is single-tier-per-reference (ER-6); the inherited layer carries no such constraint.'). Not a gap.
findings.evidence: Doc lines 210-211, read directly.

findings.topic: 5. Presupposition sweep — aggregate/read-time computation
findings.fact: Ambiguous framing worth flagging rather than deciding: `aggregateEntity` (the function that materializes property buckets, §1, AND that runs the `_inheritrights` parent-fetch cascade cited as ER-7's evidence at aggregate.js:166-183/185-209) is itself described by §1 as running at WRITE time ('Every entity write runs aggregateEntity'). `cleanupEntity` (§2) is the READ-time step, but it only SELECTS among precomputed buckets — it does not aggregate. So the rights-tier cascade that ER-7 depends on is ALSO a write-time computation, sharing the same function as the property-bucket snapshot in §1 — yet no ER states this unification ('rights-tier arrays, like property buckets, are write-time snapshots computed by the same aggregateEntity pass') as its own rule. It is presupposed jointly by ER-6, ER-7, and ER-9 (all reason about grants 'retiring'/'combining' at write time) plus the to-be-assigned §1 foundation rule. Not citable today; tightly coupled to the §1 fix this issue requests.
findings.evidence: Doc line 33 ('Every entity write runs aggregateEntity'); ER-7 evidence citing aggregate.js:166-183,185-209 (same file/function family as §1's aggregate.js:312-320); ER-6/ER-9 (lines 206-208, 216-217) reasoning about grant replacement without stating when the combination happens.

findings.topic: 5. Presupposition sweep — JWT/caller-identity model (entu.userStr / accounts map)
findings.fact: Partially but not fully covered. ER-10 covers the DB-BOUNDARY consequence of the accounts map ('A user authenticated against install X cannot read domain entities in install Y unless they genuinely have a person entity in Y', citing middleware/auth.js:21,31-33,46-48 and routes/auth/index.get.js:132,141-190,254). But the more general mechanic that §2 (ungoverned, per finding 1) and ER-1/ER-3/ER-4 all lean on — that `entu.userStr` is the caller's own person-id in the CURRENT db, and grant-matching tests it against the entity's `access` array — has no dedicated foundational ER distinct from ER-10's boundary-specific framing. Presupposed by: §2's grant-branch (to be ID'd), ER-1 ('tier-admitted' = admitted by domain/public sharing, i.e., NOT via userStr-in-access match), ER-3/ER-4 ('grant-admitted' = admitted via userStr-in-access match), and ER-10 itself (which narrows to the cross-db case). A soft gap: the general caller-identity/grant-matching mechanic that §2 states in prose (line 47 `entu.userStr && entity.access?...includes(entu.userStr)`) has no ER of its own separate from the boundary-specific ER-10.
findings.evidence: Doc lines 47-50 (§2 code, ungoverned); ER-10 (lines 122-123); ER-1 (lines 94-96, 'tier-admitted' term); ER-4 (lines 177-178, 'grant-admitted' term).

findings.topic: 5. Presupposition sweep — rights-property write path mechanics
findings.fact: Mostly covered, minor residual gap. ER-11 already generalizes correctly ('_sharing is a rights-type property, and writing or deleting ANY rights-type property requires the caller be in the entity's _owner list') and ER-17 qualifies it (systemUser bypass, write-path only). The one un-ID'd piece is the `rightTypes` enumeration itself (which 7 properties count as rights-type) — it sits in §5 prose (line 131) OUTSIDE any blockquote, so while ER-11's rule text is general enough not to need the enumeration to be independently citable, the enumeration itself is presupposed by ER-11, ER-6, ER-9, ER-17 (all reason about a fixed small set: `_owner`/`_editor`/`_viewer`/`_expander`/`_sharing`/`_inheritrights`/`_noaccess`) with no ER covering it. This folds into the four-tier-ladder gap above (same underlying array, superset of it).
findings.evidence: §5 prose line 131 (rightTypes array); ER-11 (lines 137-139, general 'any rights-type property' wording already avoids needing a separate citation for the base rule itself).

findings.topic: 6. ER-16 exact text and whether it needs edits
findings.fact: ER-16 full text (lines 244-245): '> **ER-16** — Working notes and scratchpads cite a rule's stable identifier, never restate its content.\n> **[unverified]** as a documentation-governance convention: a stipulated discipline of this document, not an Entu mechanics fact with a source `file:line` of its own. Rationale: a restatement in a working note is exactly how the per-reference qualifier on ER-6 got lost on 2026-09-10, and leaving this instruction as unidentified prose would make it the one rule here that cannot be cited.' The rule's text is generic (about ALL rules' identifiers, not scoped to any specific ER id or content), so adding new §1/§2 foundation IDs (ER-18/ER-19 or whatever the GREEN implementer assigns) requires zero edits to ER-16 itself — confirmed nothing in its wording needs changing.
findings.evidence: Doc lines 244-245, read directly; issue #320 body's own framing ('the librarian's entry now states this material knowingly in breach of ER-16... the fix direction is new IDs') matches — the breach is about the MISSING foundation IDs, not about ER-16's own wording.

findings.topic: 2b. Guard-spec parser tolerates added lines inside an ER block — quoted
findings.fact: parseRuleBlocks in src/rights-model-identifiers.spec.ts treats a rule block as every contiguous run of lines starting with '>' (lines 80-96): 'while (i < lines.length && lines[i].startsWith('>')) i += 1;' then slices raw = lines.slice(start, i), matches only raw[0] against DEFINITION_FIRST_LINE to capture the id, and joins ALL raw lines (stripping the leading '> ') into block.text. Adding a new '> Cross-ref: ER-18, ER-19.' line inside the ER-1 or ER-3 block (as long as it keeps the '>' prefix and sits before the blank line that ends the block) is absorbed into the same block — the parser is purely boundary-based (contiguous '>' lines), not positional or line-count-limited beyond the separately-enforced 12-line/1200-char caps (spec's own describe block 4). So a cross-ref line added inside the block is tolerated by the parser; it is NOT tolerated if it is placed after a blank line (that would start a new, id-less blockquote and simply get skipped, line 89's `continue`).
findings.evidence: src/rights-model-identifiers.spec.ts lines 76-99 (parseRuleBlocks), quoted verbatim above.
